quizzes.title: US 20-point Gaza plan: features
quizzes.passage: The Gaza war began in 2023. The United States has put forward a 20-point plan to end the war in Gaza. The plan carries the official title Comprehensive Plan to End the Gaza Conflict. It followed talks between President Donald Trump and Israel's Prime Minister, Benjamin Netanyahu. The main aim is to bring the fighting to an end and to build a stable future for Gaza and its people. The plan describes Gaza's future in broad terms, and it sets out a sequence of steps for both sides to take. Essential goods are to reach the territory without delay, and damaged infrastructure is to be rebuilt. The economy is also to be revived, with jobs created and the region rebuilt as a place to live and work. The points cover security, aid, governance and reconstruction, and together they form one framework. Political arrangements form another part of the design. Day-to-day civil administration would pass to a temporary body of Palestinians working under a wider international board. The plan also points towards self-determination and statehood for Palestinians, and the United States is to lead talks on a peaceful political future between Israelis and Palestinians. Each part of the framework is set out in a numbered point in the plan.

questions.q: According to the plan, the special economic zone for Gaza is to be supported by which source?
options: A tax on goods entering the territory
questions.explanation: The booklet says the special economic zone is supported by international investment and employment generation.

questions.q: What does the plan say about the freedom of Gaza's residents to remain or move?
options: They are free to stay, leave or return
They must remain in place until reconstruction ends
They are moved to designated camps
They are required to leave during reconstruction
questions.explanation: The plan rules out forced displacement, so residents may stay, leave or return.

questions.q: Which force is to be deployed to secure Gaza and train its police?
questions.explanation: The International Stabilization Force (ISF) is deployed to secure Gaza and train police.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The plan gives Hamas a role in governing Gaza after the war.
Reason (R): Hamas is excluded from governance under the plan.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Hamas is excluded from governance under the plan, so A is false while R is true.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
List I
I. Interfaith dialogue platform
II. Special economic zone
III. Hamas members who decommission weapons
IV. Rafah crossing
List II
A. Amnesty or safe passage abroad
B. Reopens under agreement
C. Promotes religious harmony
D. Favourable trade terms
questions.explanation: The platform promotes religious harmony, the economic zone has favourable trade terms, decommissioning brings amnesty, and Rafah reopens under agreement.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the US 20-point plan for Gaza:
I. Gaza is to become a demilitarised, terror-free zone.
II. Israeli forces are to withdraw as stability and demilitarisation progress.
III. The plan requires all Palestinian prisoners to remain in detention.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and II match the plan, while III contradicts the plan's release of detainees.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the plan's terms:
I. Israel is to free 250 Palestinian life-sentence prisoners.
II. Israel is to occupy Gaza permanently under the plan.
III. All hostages, alive or deceased, must be released within 72 hours of Israel's formal acceptance.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and III are in the booklet, while II contradicts the plan's position that Israel will not occupy Gaza.

quizzes.title: US 20-point Gaza plan: recall
quizzes.passage: A twenty-point plan has been proposed to end the war in Gaza. Its formal name is the Comprehensive Plan to End the Gaza Conflict. Its proposer had held talks with the Israeli Prime Minister before putting it forward. The plan imagines a Gaza that is free of militant activity, so that it poses no threat to neighbouring states. Its early provisions concern a halt to military operations, the release of people held by each side, and the immediate entry of aid. The aid is meant to help rebuild essential infrastructure. The plan also proposes a special economic zone with favourable trade terms, which would be supported by outside investment and would generate employment. Gaza would be governed for a time by Palestinians working under an international board. The plan also points towards self-determination and statehood for Palestinians, with a peaceful political future to be sought through talks between Israelis and Palestinians. Each of these elements is set out as one of the plan's twenty points. The wider dispute has a long history, and Britain was granted a mandate over Palestine after the First World War. Gaza is described as a place where Israel's military would withdraw as stability grows. Gaza's residents are free to stay, leave or return.

questions.q: Within how many hours of Israel's formal acceptance must all hostages, alive or deceased, be released? (hours)
questions.explanation: The plan requires release within 72 hours of Israel's formal acceptance.

questions.q: How many Palestinian life-sentence prisoners is Israel to free under the plan? (number)
questions.explanation: The plan has Israel free 250 Palestinian life-sentence prisoners, alongside 1,700 detainees.

questions.q: Which Israeli Prime Minister did the plan's proposer hold talks with before proposing it? (full name)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the plan was proposed after talks with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

questions.q: What is the abbreviation of the force deployed to secure Gaza and train its police? (abbreviation)
questions.explanation: The International Stabilization Force (ISF) is deployed to secure Gaza and train police.

questions.q: Which country leads the talks on a peaceful political future between Israelis and Palestinians? (country)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the US leads talks for a peaceful political future between Israel and the Palestinians.

questions.q: What kind of platform does the plan create to promote religious harmony? (two words)
questions.explanation: The plan creates an Interfaith Dialogue Platform to promote religious harmony.

questions.q: What kind of committee temporarily governs Gaza under the plan? (one word)
questions.explanation: The plan has Gaza governed temporarily by a technocratic Palestinian committee under an international board.

quizzes.title: Board of Peace: UN reform and significance
quizzes.passage: A current affairs account treats reform of the United Nations system as urgent. Its argument begins with efforts to rebuild societies after conflict. Peacebuilding efforts often suffer from fragmentation and a loss of institutional continuity. In this setting, the Board of Peace is introduced as a US-led intergovernmental body with a transitional role in post-conflict Gaza. It works alongside the National Committee for the Administration of Gaza and the International Stabilization Force, supervising them and mobilising financial and technical assistance. The Board is also described as a new international body with its own charter, which covers membership rules, financial contributions and dispute redressal. Membership requires countries to consent to be bound by the charter. Membership can be rotational, and permanent membership is also available. Its stated objectives include transparency, coordination and accountability during Gaza's transition from conflict to reconstruction. Gaza's reconstruction is to be supported through a special economic zone with favourable trade terms. A Gaza Executive Board, described as a supporting operational body, coordinates activities on the ground. Day-to-day civil administration is handled by a committee of politically independent Palestinian technocrats. The plan also includes an interfaith dialogue platform. The wider dispute has a long history, and Britain was granted a mandate over Palestine after the First World War.

questions.q: What has the prolonged deadlock over comprehensive UN Security Council reform done?
options: Expanded the veto powers of permanent members
Made the General Assembly the sole decision-maker
questions.explanation: The booklet says the prolonged deadlock over comprehensive Security Council reform has paralysed timely action.

questions.q: What does the Board of Peace aim to institutionalise?
questions.explanation: The booklet says the Board aims to institutionalise long-term political engagement.

questions.q: How does the booklet describe the Board's innovation within the UN system?
options: A revolutionary replacement of existing bodies
An incremental innovation within existing structures
questions.explanation: The booklet calls the Board an incremental innovation working within existing structures rather than a replacement.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The General Assembly can establish subsidiary bodies without amending the UN Charter.
Reason (R): Article 22 of the UN Charter gives the General Assembly this power.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Article 22 is the provision that lets the General Assembly create subsidiary bodies without a Charter amendment, so R explains A.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
List I
I. Ad hoc peacebuilding missions
II. The Board of Peace
III. The Board's stated purpose
IV. The Board's decision-making style
List II
A. End once immediate crises subside
B. Reform from within, not replacement
C. Preventing relapse into conflict
D. Rapid decision-making over consensus-based diplomacy
questions.explanation: Ad hoc missions end once crises subside, the Board is reform from within, its purpose is preventing relapse, and its style favours rapid decisions over consensus.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements on the Board's role and design:
I. The Board of Peace is presented as a replacement for the UN Security Council.
II. The Board is said to signal evolving US thinking on conflict resolution.
III. The Board is projected as a template for managing complex global conflicts.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement I is false because the Board is presented as reform from within, not a replacement for the Security Council.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Board's approach to global governance:
I. The Board represents a move towards mini-lateral, leader-centric mechanisms.
II. The Board emphasises consensus-based diplomacy over rapid decision-making.
III. UN peacebuilding missions often continue long after immediate crises subside.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Only statement I matches the booklet, since the Board stresses rapid decisions and missions usually end once crises subside.

quizzes.title: Board of Peace: UN reform recall
quizzes.passage: A current affairs account treats reform of the United Nations system as urgent. Peacebuilding efforts often suffer from fragmentation and a loss of institutional continuity. The Charter already allows a route for change, because the General Assembly may create subsidiary bodies without amending the Charter itself. This makes change faster than a full amendment process would be. The Board of Peace is presented as an example of this kind of innovation. It is described as a US-led intergovernmental body set up for Gaza's transition from conflict to reconstruction. It supervises a national committee for Gaza's administration and a stabilisation force, while mobilising international financial and technical assistance. The account stresses that the Board is meant to operate within existing arrangements rather than in opposition to them. The Board is intended to ensure transparency, coordination and accountability. Membership requires countries to consent to be bound by the charter. A Gaza Executive Board, described as a supporting operational body, coordinates activities on the ground. The account also notes that the Board signals changing thinking on how conflicts are resolved. Membership can be rotational, and permanent membership is also available. The wider dispute has a long history, and Britain was granted a mandate over Palestine after the First World War.

questions.q: Under which Article of the UN Charter can the General Assembly set up subsidiary bodies without amending the Charter? (number)
questions.explanation: Article 22 lets the General Assembly establish subsidiary bodies without a Charter amendment.

questions.q: Moving away from universal multilateral institutions, the Board is described as a shift towards what kind of mechanisms? (one word)
questions.explanation: The booklet describes the Board as a move towards mini-lateral, leader-centric mechanisms.

questions.q: By institutionalising long-term political engagement, what does the Board aim to prevent? (one word)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the Board aims to prevent relapse into conflict.

questions.q: Which kind of missions often end once immediate crises subside? (two words)
questions.explanation: The booklet notes that ad hoc missions end once immediate crises subside, which weakens continuity.

questions.q: The Board emphasises rapid decision-making over which type of diplomacy? (one word)
questions.explanation: The Board stresses rapid decision-making over consensus-based diplomacy.

questions.q: The Board is projected as a template for managing what kind of conflicts? (one word)
questions.explanation: The booklet projects the Board as a template for managing complex global conflicts.

questions.q: The Board is presented as reform from within rather than a replacement of which UN organ? (abbreviation)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the Board does not undermine or replace the UNSC but seeks to strengthen coordination.
